linksquares.detail: The same searches returned no evidence of any patent-litigation feature.

draftwise.detail: Not found; searches returned only generic patent-prosecution background, no DraftWise-specific results.

genie-ai.detail: Not found; the same searches returned no company-specific hits.

ktmine.detail: No dedicated IPR/PTAB workflow was found; the Benchmark App mentions general litigation support for law firms around royalty benchmarking only.

ipwe.detail: No mention found in press coverage or search snippets, and the company's own site could not be reached directly to confirm either way.

deepip.detail: The Invalidity Search product generates sourced invalidity claim charts that functionally align with IPR prep, but the product isn't explicitly branded as an IPR/PTAB-named workflow.

junior.detail: No mention found; product scope is patent drafting plus office-action response only.

ankar-ai.detail: The Claim Charts product states charts are used across prosecution, litigation, and post-grant proceedings, implying IPR/PTAB use, but there's no dedicated IPR/PTAB-named workflow.

patented-ai.detail: The site explicitly markets "court-proven, IPR-grade source code analysis to invalidate patents" under its litigation section.

xlscout.detail: The Invalidator LLM explicitly assesses IPR vulnerability and produces invalidity summaries positioned as inputs for IPR petitions or defense.

nlpatent.detail: The same coverage confirms invalidity workflows, a prerequisite for IPR support, are not yet released.

patentpal.detail: No evidence found in any source searched. The company's main site blocked direct fetching, so this row relies on third-party reviews and cached subpages rather than the vendor's own copy.

amplified-ai.detail: The company published benchmarking of its retrieval against PTAB IPR-challenged patents showing IPR relevance, but no named PTAB/IPR module was found — it appears folded into general invalidity search.

iprova.detail: No evidence found in any source searched.

minesoft.detail: A targeted search for a Minesoft PTAB/IPR module surfaced no dedicated litigation-support feature on any product page.

questel.detail: A "Prosecution Pack" product provides PTAB final-decision statistics by examiner, law firm, and applicant.

park-ip.detail: Its litigation page confirms services are translation, interpreting, and e-discovery only, not substantive IPR/PTAB analysis.

patseer.detail: General invalidity-search tooling applies to IPR prep, but no page names a dedicated PTAB/IPR workflow specifically.

patently.detail: The "Shape" module supports prosecution, oppositions, and litigation workflows generally, but no page names IPR or PTAB specifically.

ip-author.detail: No dedicated PTAB or IPR page or mention was found.

powerpatent.detail: No evidence found; the product is founder/startup-focused drafting and prosecution, not litigation.

cypris.detail: The API layer can query USPTO's PTAB data as a raw data source, but this is API/data access rather than a dedicated in-product litigation-support workflow.

claim-charting.author: Patent Attorney, Mid-size Firm
claim-charting.text: The claim charting is genuinely fast once you've mapped the claim elements — cut a task that used to take an associate a full day down to about an hour of review.

claim-charting.author: u/claims_examiner_throwaway
claim-charting.text: Solve's chart output is good for a first pass, but I still had to manually fix a couple of citation mappings that were close but not quite right.

office-action-response.author: IP Paralegal
office-action-response.text: The v2 office-action drafting update is a real improvement — the claim-amendment suggestions actually track the examiner's rejection language now.

prior-art-search.author: R&D Program Manager
prior-art-search.text: Search coverage is huge — great for landscaping. It's less good at surfacing the one obscure reference you actually needed for a novelty opinion.

portfolio-analytics.author: Director of IP Operations
portfolio-analytics.text: The portfolio dashboards are the reason we kept renewing — good for board-level reporting on filing trends across business units.

prior-art-search.author: Patent Search Specialist
prior-art-search.text: The graph-based approach actually found prior art our classification-code search missed on two separate projects this quarter. Worth the switch.

fto-analysis.author: u/fto_grind
fto-analysis.text: Good for FTO first passes but you still need a human to sanity-check claim scope on anything with means-plus-function language.

claim-charting.author: In-house Patent Counsel
claim-charting.text: It's fine for internal review but the output isn't polished enough to hand to opposing counsel or a court without reformatting.

claim-charting.author: Licensing Manager
claim-charting.text: We use this mainly for building licensing packages — the claim charts are geared toward monetization conversations, not litigation-grade detail.
